result.title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
result.summary: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly used to automate biomedical research, creating a growing need to benchmark their capabilities on real scientific data and workflows. Their reliability in neuroimaging remains insufficiently characterized, where plausible analytical outputs can conceal errors that affect scientific conclusions. Existing studies have advanced scientific question answering and tool-based automation, but provide limited evidence on workflow reconstruction, acquisition of procedural expertise and evidence-based scientific judgment. Here we present NIBench, a neuroimaging benchmark comprising three complementary evaluations of autonomous agents. First, we benchmark execution and workflow reconstruction using 56 tasks across seven tool ecosystems, covering structural, diffusion and functional magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography and multimodal analyses. Second, we examine whether agents can evolve their procedural skills through distillation of execution trajectories, evaluating the resulting skills on previously encountered tasks, unseen tasks and other models. Third, we assess scientific judgment using 36 claims from published Alzheimer's disease studies, requiring agents to analyse raw cohort data and provide reproducible evidence. We evaluate 19 language models within a shared agent framework, with selected models undergoing skill distillation and claim evaluation. Leading agents execute supplied analysis protocols nearly perfectly, whereas withholding procedural guidance widens performance differences. Distilled skills improve performance on acquisition tasks and transfer between models, but benefits on unseen tasks are inconsistent. Agents reproduce their reported results yet sometimes reach conclusions inconsistent with expert-derived answers, and access to data does not always improve judgment.

AI.brief_summary: NIBench 是面向神经影像科研智能体的基准，包含 56 个流程复现任务（覆盖七个工具生态）、由执行轨迹蒸馏技能并测试其向未见任务与其他模型的迁移，以及基于 36 条阿尔茨海默病研究结论的可复现证据判断评测，共比较 19 个语言模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「轨迹蒸馏获得程序性技能并检验迁移泛化」与「有数据访问未必改善判断」的诊断思路，可供核查 LVR 中轨迹监督的贡献分配及视觉证据是否真被使用；但对象是高层影像流程代理，与内部 latent 表示无直接关系，联系需较多核查。
